Method of Attack: Malicious ads serve exploit code targeting vulnerable routers instead of browsers to insert ads on all visited sites
Malicious JavaScript in ads uses WebRTC to get local IP and identify routers on local networks
Exploit kit sends encrypted payloads using AES keys embedded via steganography in images
Tests victim routers against a list of 166 router fingerprints to identify vulnerable models
Delivers exploit packages containing vulnerabilities or hardcoded admin credentials to take over routers and change DNS settings
Attempts to open router administration ports for external control in some cases
Uses compromised routers to replace or insert ads in user traffic on desktop and mobile devices
Impacted Systems: Routers from brands including Linksys, Netgear, D-Link, Comtrend, Pirelli, Zyxel
Routers matching 166 known fingerprints targeted by the exploit kit
Attack Vector: Malicious advertisements on legitimate websites containing JavaScript
Browser-based WebRTC requests to identify local network routers
Redirects from tainted ads to exploit kit landing pages
Hidden HTML iframes executing exploit code out of user sight
